items.title: Hikers rescued after using Google Gemini for planning
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: <article>The sheriff’s office said the hikers “were advised by Gemini to bring far less food and water than their group required."</article>

items.title: OpenAI confirms ‘wiki incident,’ says it’s ‘working on a framework’ for more disclosure
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: <article>OpenAI acknowledged its role in a recently reported incident where AI agents took over a German wiki forum.</article>

items.title: Clucky’s new alarm app wakes you up with a crowing rooster
items.author: Lauren Forristal
items.content: <article>Clucky's new alarm app has an option where users are woken up to the sound of a rooster. They then complete a mission to turn it off. </article>

items.title: Oura is going public, but these smart ring companies are coming for its crown
items.author: Aisha Malik
items.content: <article>While Oura has largely dominated the smart ring market for years, a growing number of rivals are now racing to dethrone it by trying all sorts of approaches to get an edge over it.</article>

items.title: XDOF, just three months out of stealth, is in talks for a Series B at a $1.2B valuation
items.author: Marina Temkin
items.content: <article>The round is being raised just months after the robot data startup exited from stealth. </article>

items.title: OpenAI’s rogue agents keep escaping, with no formal process to investigate them
items.author: Rebecca Bellan
items.content: <article>OpenAI’s latest agent swarm incident adds urgency to calls for independent investigations as researchers and lawmakers question whether AI labs should control the scope of their own safety reviews.</article>

items.title: AI compute provider Nscale is looking for $3.5B in pre-IPO financing
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: <article>Nscale, which recently struck a $45 billion deal with Anthropic, is in talks to raise additional funds in anticipation of an upcoming IPO. </article>

items.title: Judge blocks X rival from using Twitter name, but allows ‘Tweet’ for now
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: <article>A federal judge temporarily barred an X rival from using the Twitter name, but found that X was likely to have abandoned the “Tweet” trademark and bird logo. The startup has since relaunched as Tweet.app.</article>

items.title: What will Apple’s John Ternus era look like?
items.author: Theresa Loconsolo
items.content: <article>It’s officially the Ternus era at Apple.   Tim Cook stepped down as CEO this week, handing the company to former hardware chief John Ternus, whose first memo promised a “huge launch next week” — timing that puts Apple’s next iPhone event on his desk before he’s even settled in. Cook isn’t going far, though: he’s staying on as Executive Chairman, focused on the kind of policy […]</article>

items.title: No little kids allowed, and other new info about Tesla’s Cybercab
items.author: Sean O'Kane
items.content: <article>The company says no children under 13 can ride -- even with a parent. That's more restrictive than the Model Y SUVs it's using as robotaxis.</article>

items.title: Another swarm of OpenAI agents reached the open internet without the frontier lab’s knowledge
items.author: Tim Fernholz
items.content: <article>It's the latest failure of OpenAI's internal monitoring and security systems.</article>

items.title: CD sales are making an unexpected comeback amid a retro tech boom
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: <article>U.S. CD revenue jumped 58.6% in the first half of 2026, reversing last year’s decline as interest in retro tech and physical media continues to grow.</article>

items.title: Krafton doubles down on India with another $250M bet beyond gaming
items.author: Jagmeet Singh
items.content: <article>Krafton's planned investment in India is set to surpass $500 million with its latest commitment.</article>

items.title: Google’s Gemini Spark can now manage your Google Photos library
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: <article>Gemini Spark can edit and curate photo albums, create shared collections, turn photos into calendar events, and handle other Google Photos tasks for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.</article>

items.title: Less than 24 hours to apply for your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Side Event
items.author: TechCrunch Events
items.content: <article>Less than 24 hours left to apply to host a Side Event during TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 and make your mark in the Silicon Valley scene. Apply before the application closes tonight at midnight PT.</article>

items.title: US military disabled ad tracking on troops’ devices following reports of targeted attacks
items.author: Zack Whittaker
items.content: <article>A senator's letter confirms the U.S. military moved to prevent the tracking after foreign adversaries used location data to target troops.</article>

items.title: Feds launch investigation into Tesla’s Cybercab deployment
items.author: Sean O'Kane, Kirsten Korosec
items.content: <article>The investigation was launched just a few hours after Tesla put the first production Cybercabs on the road in Austin.</article>

items.title: The sameness problem behind those unappetizing AI-generated menus
items.author: Amanda Silberling
items.content: <article>While restaurant owners might look to generative AI as a shortcut to sprucing up their menu, customers can viscerally sense that something is wrong with the food.</article>

items.title: Crusoe reportedly raises $3B at a $30B valuation
items.author: Marina Temkin
items.content: <article>The round came together after the data center developer reportedly secured a $13 billion contract with Jane Street.</article>

items.title: Oura files to go public
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: <article>The ring maker says that its business has shown significant revenue growth over the past year. </article>
